title: CommandList
description: A list of FElupe Studio commands. Objects are created by commands and referenced by their names.

Name.description: Name of an object, unique within the command list. Used as a Python identifier in the generated script; at most 24 characters keep the script readable.

x-reserved.$comment: Names that must not be used, because the generated script uses them (felupe_studio.codegen). Checked by felupe_studio.commands and app/src/core/validate.ts.

Coordinates.description: The coordinates x, y and z of a point.

MeshImport.description: Import a mesh file (read with meshio).

file.description: File name of the mesh, e.g. specimen.vtu.

tag.description: Name of an integer cell data array used to split the mesh into cell sets, e.g. material or gmsh:physical.

cell_type.description: Type of the solid cells to import, if the file has more than one (one mesh per cell type).

scale.description: Factor of the coordinates of the points, e.g. 1000 for a mesh in m of a model in mm. The points are multiplied after reading, before the cell sets; point sets and points are in the scaled coordinates.

MeshScript.description: A mesh made by a Python script next to the project, e.g. with the mesh tools of FElupe. The script runs with the parameters of the model as variables and makes a variable mesh: a fem.Mesh, a fem.MeshContainer, a meshio.Mesh or a dict of names and meshes (one mesh object per item).

file.description: File name of the script, e.g. bushing.py.

parameters.description: The parameters of the model that the script gets as variables (default: all).

item.description: The item of a dict of meshes, e.g. rubber.

tag.description: Name of an integer cell data array of a meshio.Mesh used to split the mesh into cell sets.

cell_type.description: Type of the solid cells to take, if the mesh has more than one.

ModelSettings.description: The settings of the model, at most once. The units say what the numbers mean: FElupe has no units, nothing is converted.

analysis.description: The type of the model: 3D (the default) or 2D, as plane strain (fem.FieldPlaneStrain, the forces per unit thickness) or axisymmetric (fem.FieldAxisymmetric: x is the axis of rotation, y the radius, the forces are the totals over the circumference). A 2D model has 2D cells (triangles and quads) and the components x and y.

units.description: The units of lengths and forces, which give the units of the stresses (e.g. mm and N give MPa). Without units, the numbers have none.

length.description: Unit of the coordinates and the displacements.

ParameterAdd.description: A parameter of the model: a number, e.g. a dimension or the number of cells of a mesh made by a script. The generated script defines it as a variable at its top.

quantity.description: The physical quantity of the value, for its unit of the model settings (e.g. mm for a length). Without it, the value has no unit.

step.description: The step of the value, e.g. of a slider.

integer.description: The value is an integer, e.g. a number of layers or cells (default false); the range and the step are integers too.

description.description: What the parameter is, in a few words, e.g. Radius of the rubber disc.

MeshMerge.description: Merge points of the sections whose coordinates agree to the given number of decimals (fem.field.merge(..., decimals)). Without this command, only identical points are merged. Merged points take the rounded coordinates.

decimals.description: Number of decimals of the point coordinates compared for merging, e.g. 6.

CellSetFromTag.description: Cell set of all cells of a mesh with the given tag value.

value.description: Value of the tag of the cells, e.g. 1.

CellSetFromFile.description: Cell set of all cells of a mesh.

MaterialAdd.description: Add a material to the material library. Every model is a definition below (the material registry): its label, the FElupe class or tensortrax function, and its parameters with label, description, bounds and default.

MaterialNeoHooke.description: Isotropic hyperelastic Neo-Hookean material (fem.NeoHooke). Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialMooneyRivlin.description: Isotropic hyperelastic Mooney-Rivlin material (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.mooney_rivlin, needs tensortrax). The shear modulus is 2 (C10 + C01). Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

C10.description: Material parameter of the first invariant

C01.description: Material parameter of the second invariant

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialYeoh.description: Isotropic hyperelastic Yeoh material (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.yeoh, needs tensortrax): a cubic polynomial of the first invariant. The shear modulus is 2 C10. Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

C10.description: Material parameter of the linear term of the first invariant

C20.description: Material parameter of the quadratic term of the first invariant

C30.description: Material parameter of the cubic term of the first invariant

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialThirdOrderDeformation.description: Isotropic hyperelastic third-order deformation material (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.third_order_deformation, needs tensortrax): terms of the first and second invariant up to the third order. The shear modulus is 2 (C10 + C01). Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

C10.description: Material parameter of the linear term of the first invariant

C01.description: Material parameter of the linear term of the second invariant

C11.description: Material parameter of the mixed term of the first and second invariant

C20.description: Material parameter of the quadratic term of the first invariant

C30.description: Material parameter of the cubic term of the first invariant

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialOgden.description: Isotropic hyperelastic Ogden material (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.ogden, needs tensortrax): up to three terms of the principal stretches, each with a modulus μi and an exponent αi. The shear modulus is the sum of the moduli. Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

mu.description: Moduli of the terms, one to three, as many as exponents

alpha.description: Stretch exponents of the terms, one per modulus, not zero

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialArrudaBoyce.description: Isotropic hyperelastic Arruda-Boyce material, the eight-chain model (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.arruda_boyce, needs tensortrax). The chains lock at the limiting stretch. Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

C1.description: Shear modulus of the chain network (the initial shear modulus for a large limiting stretch)

limit.description: Limiting stretch at which the chains are locked

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialExtendedTube.description: Isotropic hyperelastic extended tube material of Kaliske and Heinrich (fem.Hyperelastic with fem.extended_tube, needs tensortrax): a cross-link and a tube constraint contribution. The shear modulus is Gc + Ge. Without a bulk modulus it needs the u-p-J formulation.

bulk.description: Bulk modulus. Without it, the material is incompressible and needs the u-p-J formulation.

MaterialLinearElasticLargeStrain.description: Linear-elastic material formulated for large deformations (fem.LinearElasticLargeStrain).

SectionAdd.description: Assign a material and a formulation to a cell set. Each section becomes a solid body.

formulation.description: u: displacement field only. u-p-J: mixed fields (fem.FieldsMixed) for nearly incompressible materials.

bulk.description: Bulk modulus of the nearly incompressible formulation (required for u-p-J).

volumetric.description: The volumetric part U(J) of the strain energy of the u-p-J formulation with the bulk modulus K (fem.NearlyIncompressible): volume-ratio K/2 (J - 1)², stretch 9K/2 (J^(1/3) - 1)² or log K/2 ln(J)².

PointSetAdd.description: Points of the merged mesh selected by a plane, at a bound of the meshes, on a cylinder, by the coordinates of points or by point ids.

oneOf.description: Points with the given coordinate, e.g. x == 0.
Points at the smallest or largest coordinate of the meshes of the sections, e.g. z == max (without the control points). They follow a mesh whose size changes.

bound.description: The smallest (min) or the largest (max) coordinate.

oneOf.description: Points on a cylinder: at the distance radius from the line through the center parallel to the axis, e.g. a sleeve of a bushing.

axis.description: The direction of the axis of the cylinder.

center.description: A point on the axis of the cylinder (default: the origin).

oneOf.description: The points at the given coordinates, one point each, e.g. picked nodes. A coordinate without a point is an error of the script.
Points given by their ids, e.g. picked in the viewer.

PointAdd.description: A control point that is not a node of the meshes, e.g. the center point of a multi-point constraint. It is a point set of one point: all control points form a mesh of vertices that is merged with the fields of the sections.

RigidAdd.description: A rigid surface (#219): a reference point with a plane or a cylinder. The reference point is a vertex like the control points and a point set of one point, so boundaries move the surface; it does not rotate. Contacts connect points of the model to it.

coordinates.description: The reference point: a point of the plane, or of the axis of the cylinder.

oneOf.description: A plane through the reference point.

normal.description: The outward normal of the plane, towards the points that touch it.

oneOf.description: A cylinder whose axis goes through the reference point.

axis.description: The direction of the axis of the cylinder.

inside.description: The points are inside the cylinder (a tube around them), else outside (a roller).

FaceSetAdd.description: Faces of the boundary of a section, e.g. for a pressure: on a plane, or the faces with the given centers (picked in the viewport). The script makes a boundary region of the faces and a field of it, linked to the merged field. Faces of tetrahedrons have no boundary region in FElupe 12.

section.description: The section whose boundary has the faces.

oneOf.description: The faces of the boundary on a plane with the given coordinate, e.g. z == 20.

atol.description: Absolute tolerance of the coordinates of the points (default 1e-8).

oneOf.description: The faces of the boundary with the given centers (the mean of the points of a face), e.g. picked faces. A center without a face is an error of the script.

atol.description: Absolute tolerance of the centers (default 1e-6 of the size of the section).

BoundaryAdd.description: Prescribe displacement components of a point set (fem.Boundary).

constrained.description: Constrained displacement components; all others are free.

value.description: Prescribed displacement of the constrained components (default 0); a rotation in rad at a rotation point.

LoadcaseAdd.description: A load case of FElupe (fem.dof) on the merged field: the boundaries of a standard test. It is referenced like a boundary: a step ramps its moving end faces, a job records the reaction force of its (first) moving end face.

LoadcaseUniaxial.description: Uniaxial tension or compression along an axis (fem.dof.uniaxial). The end face at the largest coordinate moves.

clamped.description: Rigid end faces: no transversal displacements of the moving (and, without symmetry, the opposite) end faces.

symmetry.description: Symmetry planes at x = 0, y = 0 and z = 0 (a quarter or an eighth of a model). Without them, the opposite end faces are at the smallest coordinates.

LoadcaseBiaxial.description: Equi-biaxial tension along two axes (fem.dof.biaxial). The end faces at the largest coordinates move.

axis.description: First direction of the loading (default x).

second.description: Second direction of the loading (default y).

clamped.description: Rigid end faces: no transversal displacements of the moving (and, without symmetry, the opposite) end faces.

symmetry.description: Symmetry planes at x = 0, y = 0 and z = 0 (a quarter or an eighth of a model). Without them, the opposite end faces are at the smallest coordinates.

LoadcasePlanar.description: Planar (pure shear) tension along an axis with a constant width along a second axis (fem.dof.biaxial without a move of the second axis).

second.description: Direction of the constant width (default y).

clamped.description: Rigid end faces: no transversal displacements of the moving (and, without symmetry, the opposite) end faces.

symmetry.description: Symmetry planes at x = 0, y = 0 and z = 0 (a quarter or an eighth of a model). Without them, the opposite end faces are at the smallest coordinates.

LoadcaseShear.description: Simple shear between the end faces normal to an axis (fem.dof.shear). The face at the largest coordinate moves along the shear direction.

normal.description: Normal of the sheared end faces (default y).

compression.description: Displacement of the moving face along the normal, held during the shear (default 0).

symmetry.description: Symmetry plane normal to the third axis at its zero coordinate.

SymmetryAdd.description: Symmetry planes normal to x, y or z (fem.dof.symmetry): on a plane, the displacement component normal to it is zero and the components in the plane are free. A half, a quarter or an eighth of a model, without a load case.

axes.description: The normals of the symmetry planes.

x.description: Coordinate of the plane normal to x (default 0), only with x in axes.

y.description: Coordinate of the plane normal to y (default 0), only with y in axes.

z.description: Coordinate of the plane normal to z (default 0), only with z in axes.

MpcAdd.description: A multi-point constraint (fem.MultiPointConstraint): the points of a point set follow a center point rigidly, connected by a penalty. With a rotation point, they also rotate about the center point.

points.description: The point set of the connected points.

center.description: The center point: a control point or a point set of one point.

constrained.description: The connected components (skip the others). All of them with a rotation point.

multiplier.description: The penalty of the relative displacements (default 1000).

rotation.description: The rotation point: a control point or a point set of one point, whose values are the rotations about the center point in rad (its coordinates are not used).

ContactAdd.description: A contact of points with a rigid surface (#220): fem.ContactRigidPlane or fem.ContactRigidCylinder, an item of the steps like the constraints. The penalty of the contact is a factor of the mean stiffness of the solid bodies at the points.

points.description: The points that may touch the surface: a point set, or the points of a face set.

friction.description: The Coulomb friction coefficient (default 0, without friction).

multiplier.description: The factor of the penalty of the contact, times the mean stiffness of the solid bodies at the points (default 1).

elastic_slip.description: The allowable elastic slip of sticking points (default none: a constant tangential penalty), e.g. 0.5 % to 1 % of the size of a cell.

PressureAdd.description: A pressure on the faces of a face set (fem.SolidBodyPressure), an item of the steps: a force per deformed area, normal to the faces. A positive pressure pushes onto the faces, a negative one pulls. A ramp of a step scales the pressure.

faces.description: The face set of the pressure.

pressure.description: The pressure; positive pushes onto the faces.

LoadAdd.description: A point load (fem.PointLoad): a force at every point of a point set or at a control point, an item of the steps. A ramp of a step scales the force.

points.description: The point set or the control point of the load.

force.description: The force fx, fy, fz at every point.

StepAdd.description: A step with all boundaries, optionally ramping items, each with its own values (fem.Step).

sections.description: Sections whose solid bodies are items of the step (default: all).

constraints.description: Multi-point constraints that are items of the step (default: all).

loads.description: Point loads and pressures that are items of the step (default: all).

ramp.description: Ramp the values of items with fem.math.linsteps([start, end], num), with the same number of increments for all items.

items.description: The ramped items, each with its own values.

RampItem.description: A ramped item: a boundary (its value, e.g. a displacement), a load case (the displacement of its moving faces), a point load (a factor of its force) or a pressure (a factor of its pressure).

target.description: The ramped boundary, load case, point load or pressure.

start.description: Value at the start of the step (default 0).

end.description: Value at the end of the step.

JobAdd.description: A job evaluating steps one after another (fem.Job). With a curve, the force-displacement curve of a boundary, a load case or a point load is recorded (fem.CharacteristicCurve).

curve.description: The boundary, load case or point load of the force-displacement curve.

tol.description: Tolerance of the Newton-Raphson method: the norm of the residual forces relative to the reaction forces (default 0.01, like commercial codes).

maxiter.description: The maximum number of Newton iterations of a substep (default 16).

solver.description: The linear solver of the Newton iterations (Job.evaluate(solver=...)); without it, SuperLU of FElupe.

type.description: SuperLU of FElupe (fem.solve.SuperLUSolver, the default), spsolve of SciPy (the default of FElupe before v12) or an iterative method of SciPy.

method.description: The iterative method of scipy.sparse.linalg: minres (symmetric, also indefinite), cg (symmetric positive definite), gmres or bicgstab.

rtol.description: Relative tolerance of the iterative method, relative to the norm of the residual forces (default: the tolerance of the job / 100).

maxiter.description: The maximum number of iterations of the iterative method (default of SciPy).

cutback.description: Retry a substep that does not converge with smaller increments (fem.CutbackPlugin); without a value, a parameter has the default of FElupe.

factor.description: The factor by which the increment is reduced after a failed attempt (default 0.5).

max_cutbacks.description: The maximum number of successive cutbacks of the increment (default 10): the smallest increment of a substep is factor ** max_cutbacks.

growth.description: The factor by which the increment is increased after a converged increment (default 2.0); 1 keeps the increment.
